65042513.belief: Philosophy is just about saying what you think.
65042513.statement: Philosophy is just about saying what you think.
65042513.correction: Philosophy does involve thinking hard, but this means critically examining your ideas.

359159624.belief: Socratic questioning is just about asking difficult questions.
359159624.statement: Socratic questioning is just about asking difficult questions.
359159624.correction: Socratic questioning is a disciplined method of inquiry which includes specific question styles.

310871367.belief: Plato believed we are born knowing everything.
310871367.statement: Students might think Plato believed we are born knowing everything.
310871367.correction: Plato believed learning was a form of remembering knowledge hidden in us.

408132576.belief: Socrates, Plato and Aristotle had similar worldviews.
408132576.statement: Socrates, Plato and Aristotle had similar worldviews.
408132576.correction: Although Aristotle was Plato's student, he had quite a different worldview and believed we can gain true knowledge by observing the world around us.

124581799.belief: A blik is a belief or opinion that can be easily changed with evidence.
124581799.statement: Students might think a blik is a belief or opinion that can be easily changed with evidence.
124581799.correction: A blik is a fundamental worldview that is unchanged by evidence or facts.

143899295.belief: Not everyone has a worldview and someone's worldview is entirely their own choice.
143899295.statement: Not everyone has a worldview and someone's worldview is entirely their own choice.
143899295.correction: We may not be conscious of having a worldview but everyone stands somewhere and our worldview is influenced by many external factors.

117895591.belief: Covenants are only found in the Old Testament or Torah.
117895591.statement: Covenants are only found in the Old Testament or Torah.
117895591.correction: Many covenants are found in the Old Testament or Torah, but the new covenant is contained within the New Testament.

781006338.belief: Everyone in the Torah or Old Testament always believed in only one god.
781006338.statement: Everyone in the Torah or Old Testament always believed in only one god.
781006338.correction: Abram's family and the people of Abram's homeland were polytheists, meaning they believed in multiple gods.

612036163.belief: All Jews, Christians and Muslims practice circumcision because of the Abrahamic covenant.
612036163.statement: All Jews, Christians and Muslims practice circumcision because of the Abrahamic covenant.
612036163.correction: Not everyone who follows an Abrahamic faith will practice circumcision because of the Abrahamic covenant. Jews, Christians and Muslims place differing levels of importance on the religious practice of circumcison.

271639977.belief: Judaism, Christianity and Islam have nothing in common.
271639977.statement: Judaism, Christianity and Islam have nothing in common.
271639977.correction: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are Abrahamic faiths and all three religions can be traced back to Abraham through his sons Ishmael and Isaac and their descendants.

176149532.belief: The promised lands are only significant within Judaism.
176149532.statement: The promised lands are only significant within Judaism.
176149532.correction: The promised lands are significant for different reasons within the three Abrahamic religions.

580237710.belief: All Abrahamic religions believe that Jesus is the New covenant.
580237710.statement: All Abrahamic religions believe that Jesus is the New covenant.
580237710.correction: Jesus as the New covenant is central to Christian belief. Most Jews do not believe that Jesus is the New covenant. In Islam, Jesus is considered a prophet.

187017492.belief: Prophets are people who can tell the future.
187017492.statement: Prophets are people who can tell the future.
187017492.correction: Prophets are regarded as inspired leaders who communicate the will of God. Very few prophets are believed to foretell the future.

115117258.belief: The creation story in Genesis is unique to Christianity.
115117258.statement: The creation story in Genesis is unique to Christianity.
115117258.correction: All Abrahamic faiths share this story, with Adam as the first human.

815107594.belief: Jews, Muslims and Christians are all descended from Abraham in the same way.
815107594.statement: Jews, Muslims and Christians are all descended from Abraham in the same way.
815107594.correction: Jews and Christians trace their ancestry through Isaac to Abraham. Muslims trace their ancestry through Ismail to Abraham.

263661713.belief: Moses and Musa are two different people.
263661713.statement: Moses and Musa are two different people.
263661713.correction: Musa is the term Muslims use for Moses, translated from the Arabic.

309855587.statement: Pupils may not realise that David is seen as a prophet in the Islamic tradition.
309855587.correction: David is seen as a prophet. However, as he repented, he did not sin.

81292228.statement: Pupils might think that Muhammad communicated directly with Allah.
81292228.correction: Muslims believe that Muhammad was given the revelation of the Qur'an via an angel.

212036023.belief: The persons of the Trinity are three separate gods.
212036023.statement: The persons of the Trinity are three separate gods.
212036023.correction: Christians believe in only one God, who is represented in three distrinct persons.

569017950.belief: Jehovah's Witnesses have the same beliefs as all other Christians.
569017950.statement: Jehovah's Witnesses have the same beliefs as all other Christians.
569017950.correction: Beliefs differ across the different Christian denominations. Jehovah's Witnesses hold some beliefs that make them a unique and distinct Christian denominiation, such as their rejection of the Trinity.

788490933.belief: Martin Luther King initiated the Protestant Reformation.
788490933.statement: Martin Luther King initiated the Protestant Reformation.
788490933.correction: Martin Luther, a German monk and theologian, initiated the Protestant Reformation in the 1500s. Martin Luther King was a minister and social rights activist in America in the 1900s. They are two different people.

56899778.belief: You can't believe in both predestination and free will.
56899778.statement: You can't believe in both predestination and free will.
56899778.correction: Christians can believe in both because: 1) God knows the free choices we will make, which enables him to predestine us; 2) We have been created with a nature which predetermines us to heaven or hell, we can still act freely within this nature.

66002391.belief: All Quakers have the same beliefs and practices.
66002391.statement: All Quakers have the same beliefs and practices.
66002391.correction: Because Quakers place emphasis on personal relationships with God, beliefs and practices can differ for each individual Quaker.

517323059.belief: The Church of England and the Anglican Church are separate.
517323059.statement: The Church of England and the Anglican Church are separate.
517323059.correction: The Anglican Church originates from the Church of England. 'Anglican' is the term for Churches all over the world that are rooted in the beliefs, teachings and practices of the Church of England. The Church of England is also referred to as Anglican.

291733792.belief: Dharma means the same thing across the dharmic religions.
291733792.statement: Dharma means the same thing across the dharmic religions.
291733792.correction: The interpretation of dharma differs amongst Hindus, Buddhists and Sikhs.

498808936.belief: The 4 yogas are referring only to the physical form of yoga.
498808936.statement: The 4 yogas are referring only to the physical form of yoga.
498808936.correction: The 4 yogas refer to the paths that Hindus can follow to fulfil their dharma.

362344161.belief: Moksha is a place or is heaven.
362344161.statement: Moksha is a place or is heaven.
362344161.correction: Moksha is where the atman (soul) is reunited with Brahman (the supreme being).

290660942.correction: The Buddha is a historical figure.

321933785.belief: The jewels refer to riches or physical treasure.
321933785.statement: The jewels refer to riches or physical treasure.
321933785.correction: The jewels are highly valued principles and institutions.

358488530.belief: The concept of dharma is the same in Sikhi, Sanatana Dharma and Buddhism.
358488530.statement: The concept of dharma is the same in Sikhi, Sanatana Dharma and Buddhism.
358488530.correction: Sikh dharma is living according to the teachings of Waheguru, Guru Nanak and the nine successive Gurus.

452488659.belief: The caste system only applied to Hindus.
452488659.statement: The caste system only applied to Hindus.
452488659.correction: The caste system was applied to people of different religions.

576599468.belief: Sikh women are not as involved as men in religious and community life.
576599468.statement: Sikh women are not as involved as men in religious and community life.
576599468.correction: Sikh women have always played an active and important role, historically, as activists and modern day professionals.

220247426.belief: The Sikh diaspora are all immigrants from the Punjab region, now in India and Pakistan.
220247426.statement: The Sikh diaspora are all immigrants from the Punjab region, now in India and Pakistan.
220247426.correction: The Sikh diaspora includes many people from countries in East Africa e.g. Uganda.

901200019.belief: The kirpan is a weapon carried for violent purposes.
901200019.statement: The kirpan is a weapon carried for violent purposes.
901200019.correction: The kirpan is a ceremonial and religious article carried by initiated Khalsa Sikhs as a symbol of their duty to stand up against injustice, not to harm others. It is one of the 5 Ks that represent Sikh identity and commitment to Waheguru (God).

20974896.belief: You can only have the names 'Singh' or 'Kaur' if you are a Khalsa Sikh.
20974896.statement: You can only have the names 'Singh' or 'Kaur' if you are a Khalsa Sikh.
20974896.correction: 'Singh' and 'Kaur' have also become used as a surname.

195933477.belief: Sewa in Sikhi is limited to physical labour, especially tasks like cleaning the Gurdwara, cooking in the langar (community kitchen), or serving food.
195933477.statement: Sewa in Sikhi is limited to physical labour, especially tasks like cleaning the Gurdwara, cooking in the langar (community kitchen), or serving food.
195933477.correction: Sikhi emphasises that sewa can be of three types: physical service, mental or emotional service or material and financial service.

233982095.belief: If humans are capable of moral evil, it means they are inherently evil.
233982095.statement: If humans are capable of moral evil, it means they are inherently evil.
233982095.correction: Being capable of moral evil doesn’t mean humans are inherently evil; it suggests that humans have free will and the ability to choose both good and bad actions, depending on circumstances and influences.

542626504.belief: Kant's deontology means that actions such as killing are always wrong.
542626504.statement: Kant's deontology means that actions such as killing are always wrong.
542626504.correction: The categorical imperative doesn’t mean the same in every situation because it takes the context into account, e.g., killing is generally wrong it can be justified where the intention is to protect life.

167167018.belief: Utilitarianism does not argue that any action is acceptable as long as it makes the majority happy.
167167018.statement: Utilitarianism does not argue that any action is acceptable as long as it makes the majority happy.
167167018.correction: Utilitarianism considers both the positive and the negative outcomes to determine which action produces the best overall consequences for the greatest number of people.

42768773.belief: Situation ethics allows for any action to be justified as long as it feels loving to the individual.
42768773.statement: Situation ethics allows for any action to be justified as long as it feels loving to the individual.
42768773.correction: Situation ethics requires thoughtful consideration and aims for actions that promote selfless and agape love for the well-being of others, rather than justifying actions based on individual feelings.

466080803.belief: Virtue ethics is just about being nice or kind, so it doesn't require much thought or effort.
466080803.statement: Virtue ethics is just about being nice or kind, so it doesn't require much thought or effort.
466080803.correction: Virtue ethics is about developing a well-rounded character through reflection and experience, not just being kind, and requires practising virtues like courage and honesty to achieve flourishing (eudaimonia).

677035094.belief: If we show compassion, we can eliminate suffering entirely.
677035094.statement: If we show compassion, we can eliminate suffering entirely.
677035094.correction: While compassion can help reduce suffering, it doesn’t always eliminate it, as some suffering may be inevitable or necessary for personal growth and moral development.

485356493.belief: Non-Christians reject the existence of Jesus completely.
485356493.statement: Non-Christians reject the existence of Jesus completely.
485356493.correction: Many non-Christians, including non-religious people, do accept that Jesus existed as a person, but reject that he existed as anything more than a historical figure.

79449071.belief: All Jews reject Jesus as the Messiah.
79449071.statement: All Jews reject Jesus as the Messiah.
79449071.correction: There is a very small number of Jews, known as Messianic Jews, who regard Jesus as the Messiah.

319672502.belief: The Gospels present exactly the same stories about Jesus, just in slightly different ways.
319672502.statement: The Gospels present exactly the same stories about Jesus, just in slightly different ways.
319672502.correction: Whilst there are many similarities across the Gospel books, there are also many differences. Some of the Gospels contain stories that others do not. For example, Jesus' birth is only recorded in Matthew and Luke, not in all four of the Gospels.

613948998.belief: All Christians believe in the incarnation.
613948998.statement: All Christians believe in the incarnation.
613948998.correction: There are a small number of Christians who do not believe that Jesus was God. For example, many of Jehovah's Witnesses do not believe in the incarnation.

394690105.belief: The Old Testament is not relevant to Jesus' teachings.
394690105.statement: The Old Testament is not relevant to Jesus' teachings.
394690105.correction: Jesus developed many teachings from the Old Testament.

167870701.belief: Jesus is not important within Islam.
167870701.statement: Jesus is not important within Islam.
167870701.correction: Jesus is highly regarded within Islam as one of the greatest prophets.

193910938.correction: The Buddha is a historical figure.

723560385.correction: The Buddharupa is a focal point and reminder of the Buddha's great qualities and ability to attain enlightenment.

326870845.belief: Buddhists find it easy to develop skilful actions.
326870845.statement: Buddhists find it easy to develop skilful actions.
326870845.correction: All Buddhists have to work at developing these skills.

801267842.belief: The five precepts are a set of rules like the ten commandments.
801267842.statement: The five precepts are a set of rules like the ten commandments.
801267842.correction: They are more things to avoid to keep a positive mental state than rules to follow.

570992842.correction: Some schools of Buddhism ordain women, known as Buddhist nuns.

882261795.belief: Only monks and nuns can be classed as the Sangha referred to in the three jewels.
882261795.statement: Only monks and nuns can be classed as the Sangha referred to in the three jewels.
882261795.correction: This is incorrect, the lay Buddhist community is also part of the Sangha.

566638698.belief: The God of classical theism is distant and not involved with creation.
566638698.statement: The God of classical theism is distant and not involved with creation.
566638698.correction: For most theists whose beliefs align with classical theism, such as Christians, God is personal and active within the world and is powerful, loving and all knowing by nature.

548113980.belief: The problem of evil only causes people to doubt God's existence.
548113980.statement: The problem of evil only causes people to doubt God's existence.
548113980.correction: The problem of evil also causes some people to doubt God's nature, rather than God's existence. The inconsistent triad challenges the belief that God is omnibenevolent and omnipotent.

322146043.belief: The devil is as powerful as God.
322146043.statement: The devil is as powerful as God.
322146043.correction: The devil's power is limited and defeated through Jesus' death and resurrection.

742576454.belief: If God was all loving, all powerful and all knowing, he would not allow humans to make harmful choices.
742576454.statement: If God was all loving, all powerful and all knowing, he would not allow humans to make harmful choices.
742576454.correction: Many Christians would argue that God gave humans the gift of free will because a world with free choice and evil is better than a world without free choice; true love and goodness can only come through free choice.

373120537.belief: The story of Job shows that God causes suffering.
373120537.statement: The story of Job shows that God causes suffering.
373120537.correction: For many Christians, the story of Job shows that Satan (the devil) is one cause of suffering, but that God may allow suffering to test humans, or for a greater purpose which may be a mystery to humans.

676390031.belief: God as transcendent means that God is not involved with or close to creation.
676390031.statement: God as transcendent means that God is not involved with or close to creation.
676390031.correction: God is both transcendent (beyond the universe) and immanent (close to creation) at the same time. God's immanence is demonstrated through Jesus, the Holy Spirit, miracles and the revelation of the Bible.

461517574.belief: Religions are always to do with belief in a God or gods.
461517574.statement: Religions are always to do with belief in a God or gods.
461517574.correction: Not all religions have a belief in God or gods. For example, Buddhism does not have beliefs in God or gods.

364933050.belief: Psychological explanations for religion mean there is no "God" or a Higher Power.
364933050.statement: That psychological explanations for religion mean there is no "God" or a Higher Power.
364933050.correction: Psychological explanations can support faith as they can show how "God" or a Higher Power has designed the brain to believe.

357101738.belief: Scientific explanations for religious experiences mean there is no God or higher power involved.
357101738.statement: Scientific explanations for religious experiences mean there is no God or higher power involved.
357101738.correction: Some may argue that scientific explanations can help us understand how a God or higher power is causing religious experiences.

250950549.belief: There is a gene or section of the brain responsible for religious belief.
250950549.statement: That there is a gene or section of the brain responsible for religious belief.
250950549.correction: Genetics and the function of the brain may play a significant part in religious belief, but there is no single gene or area of the brain responsible for this.

793900369.belief: All forms of religious belief and practices will have mental health benefits.
793900369.statement: That all forms of religious belief and practices will have mental health benefits.
793900369.correction: Religion is a very broad term and different beliefs and practices will have different effects on different individuals.

730205426.belief: Psychologists today accept all of Freud's ideas on religion.
730205426.statement: That psychologists today accept all of Freud's ideas on religion.
730205426.correction: Whilst influential, many of Freud's theories on the id and religion have been discredited.

769058189.belief: Renaissance and Enlightenment thinkers gave up the belief in God.
769058189.statement: Renaissance and Enlightenment thinkers gave up the belief in God.
769058189.correction: Renaissance and Enlightenment thinkers questioned religious authority but didn't necessarily stop believing in God, focusing instead on reason and human potential.

406990617.correction: Hobbes did not reject religion outright. Instead, he argued that religious interpretations and practices should be subject to the authority of the sovereign for the sake of social order.

489027372.correction: Hobbes did not oppose all freedom, but argued that unlimited freedom in the state of nature leads to chaos.

676433562.belief: Like Hobbes, Rousseau saw the 'state of nature' as meaning without society, humans live in fear and conflict.
676433562.statement: Like Hobbes, Rousseau saw the 'state of nature' as meaning without society, humans live in fear and conflict.
676433562.correction: Rousseau's view contrasts directly with Hobbes', he described the state of nature as a time when humans were free, equal, and lived harmoniously, not chaotic or lawless.

244978896.belief: Rousseau’s social contract is an actual written agreement signed by people.
244978896.statement: Rousseau’s social contract is an actual written agreement signed by people.
244978896.correction: The social contract is a philosophical concept, not a real document, representing an idea about how societies are formed and governed.

419139881.belief: The Enlightenment was a complete rejection of Christianity.
419139881.statement: The Enlightenment was a complete rejection of Christianity.
419139881.correction: While it challenged traditional religious views, most people remained Christian, and many Enlightenment thinkers still believed in God, such as those who supported deism.

115427799.belief: James had a clear view on the existence of God.
115427799.statement: Students may think James had a clear view on the existence of God.
115427799.correction: James' investigtions led him to be agnostic and open to the idea of God rather than to be a believer.

766801043.belief: The God helmet experiment has been reliably replicated and proves that religious experiences are just caused by brain stimulation.
766801043.statement: The God helmet experiment has been reliably replicated and proves that religious experiences are just caused by brain stimulation.
766801043.correction: In reality, the experiment has not been consistently replicated, and the results have been debated.

479952353.belief: Ian McCormack’s experience is unique and proves the truth of Christianity.
479952353.statement: Ian McCormack’s experience is unique and proves the truth of Christianity.
479952353.correction: McCormack’s experience is similar to those in other religions, where people report encounters with divine beings or light, showing such experiences aren’t unique to Christianity.

262226835.belief: St Bernadette's visions were believed by everyone at the time.
262226835.statement: St Bernadette's visions were believed by everyone at the time.
262226835.correction: Many, including her family and Church authorities, questioned her mental state, and her visions were only accepted by the Church as genuine following investigation.

130115659.belief: Sufism is a branch of Islam, like Sunni and Shi'ism.
130115659.statement: Sufism is a branch of Islam, like Sunni and Shi'ism.
130115659.correction: Sufis can be either Sunni or Shi'a, athough the majority are Sunni.

115379372.belief: Atman is just like the soul in other religions.
115379372.statement: Atman is just like the soul in other religions.
115379372.correction: While atman is similar to the soul, in Hinduism, it's not only the individual self but also connected to the larger, ultimate reality (Brahman). So, it’s more than just an individual soul; it can be seen as part of everything.

72743365.belief: The Ten Commandments were only relevant at the time, or to people who follow an Abrahamic religion.
72743365.statement: The Ten Commandments were only relevant at the time, or to people who follow an Abrahamic religion.
72743365.correction: The Ten Commandments and other religious rules have influenced many laws still in place, including things such as Sunday trading laws in modern Britain.

818403485.belief: The two Commandments form part of the Ten Commandments given to Moses by God on Mount Sinai.
818403485.statement: The two Commandments form part of the Ten Commandments given to Moses by God on Mount Sinai.
818403485.correction: The two Commandments are taught by Jesus.

782662336.belief: Jesus did not believe people should follow the law.
782662336.statement: Jesus did not believe people should follow the law.
782662336.correction: Jesus believed strongly in the importance of laws and commandments, but that agape love should be used when deciding how to apply those laws and punishments.

526317001.belief: Halal and haram just applies to food and dietary laws.
526317001.statement: Halal and haram just applies to food and dietary laws.
526317001.correction: Anything that is acceptable or forbidden in Islam is known as halal and haram.

728729519.belief: All Muslims will come to the same conclusion about a moral or social issue.
728729519.statement: All Muslims will come to the same conclusion about a moral or social issue.
728729519.correction: Different scholars will interpret sources differently meaning there is a diversity of opinion about issues such as the Eid moon sighting, and wearing of trousers and beards.

701314898.belief: All Muslims think that music is haram or forbidden.
701314898.statement: All Muslims think that music is haram or forbidden.
701314898.correction: There is a diversity of Islamic worldviews regarding whether music can be listened to and the types of music that are permissible.

248021725.belief: Martin Luther King was an important figure in the Protestant Reformation.
248021725.statement: That Martin Luther King was an important figure in the Protestant Reformation.
248021725.correction: Martin Luther King lived in the 20th century, but was named after Martin Luther who lived in the 16th century when the Protestant Reformation happened.

468504431.belief: Reaching heaven by faith alone means that works and deeds do not matter in that understanding of Christianity.
468504431.statement: That reaching heaven by faith alone means that works and deeds do not matter in that understanding of Christianity.
468504431.correction: Good works and deeds are still important even though they do not help a person reach heaven. In this understanding of Christianity, these actions and deeds come about because of faith and show the faith is genuine.

860417799.belief: Bonhoeffer was an absolute pacifist for his whole life.
860417799.statement: Bonhoeffer was an absolute pacifist for his whole life.
860417799.correction: Bonhoeffer was a pacifist, but had the opportunity to help with the attempt to assassinate Hitler, which he decided he should try to do, given the great evil and injustice Hitler was causing.

568793224.belief: The laws of a country are always based on fairness and equality.
568793224.statement: The laws of a country are always based on fairness and equality.
568793224.correction: Sometimes the laws of a country are not fair or just, for example, Apartheid and segregation were supported by laws in the USA and South Africa.

310150668.belief: Vandana Shiva opposes all types of farming.
310150668.statement: Vandana Shiva opposes all types of farming.
310150668.correction: Vandana Shiva supports farming methods which respect nature and biodoversity.

452076181.belief: Ahimsa only refers to non-violence towards humans.
452076181.statement: Ahimsa only refers to non-violence towards humans.
452076181.correction: Ahimsa refers to non-violence towards all living things, as all living things have value, worth and are interconnected.

208401809.belief: The census tells us how many people follow a religion in England and Wales.
208401809.statement: The census tells us how many people follow a religion in England and Wales.
208401809.correction: The census can only tell us what people ticked in the census. This may not be the reality.

452716025.belief: All Christians have the same beliefs and practices.
452716025.statement: That all Christians have the same beliefs and practices.
452716025.correction: There may be some core beliefs and practices that almost all Christians share but there is also a great diversity.

85094974.correction: Data shows that there are nones that are theists.

184243451.belief: Agnostics have 'nothing in common' with religious people.
184243451.statement: That agnostics have 'nothing in common' with religious people.
184243451.correction: Agnostics have much in common with religious people and some people who have an agnostic faith stance identify as religious.

713499685.belief: There is only one form of Paganism.
713499685.statement: That there is only one form of Paganism.
713499685.correction: Paganism is not one set religion or pathway but an umbrella term used for various nature based religious traditions including Wicca, Druidry and Shamanism, among others.

116126368.belief: The census data for England and Wales shows that all religious groups are 'declining' in numbers.
116126368.statement: The census data for England and Wales shows that all religious groups are 'declining' in numbers.
116126368.correction: The census data shows that Christianity has less numbers overall but other religious groups, e.g Islam, and particular groups within Christianity are increasing in numbers.

443504756.belief: There is only one interpretation of Genesis passages linked to creation.
443504756.statement: Students might think that there is only one interpretation of Genesis passages linked to creation.
443504756.correction: Genesis passages can be interpreted to argue for either dominion or stewardship. Most Christians in the UK today take a stewardship interpretation.

815367780.belief: Islam doesn't have much to say about environmental ethics.
815367780.statement: Students may think that Islam doesn't have much to say about environmental ethics.
815367780.correction: Islamic teachings provide a strong and ancient vision for sustainable living.

429946880.belief: Jewish ethics are concerned with people and not the natural world.
429946880.statement: Jewish ethics are concerned with people and not the natural world.
429946880.correction: Care for the planet and the environment is found throughout Jewish teaching and has deep roots.

75899908.belief: The Roman Catholic Church is only focused on Catholics and personal morality.
75899908.statement: The Roman Catholic Church is only focused on Catholics and personal morality.
75899908.correction: This encyclical is addressed to the whole world as Pope Francis saw that all the world was a common home for everyone.

340441220.belief: Philosophers only think about moral issues related to humans.
340441220.statement: Philosophers only think about moral issues related to humans.
340441220.correction: Some philosophers also consider animals and what level of conciousness or sentience they may have.

310917063.belief: Philosophy is just abstract thinking and doesn’t apply to everyday life.
310917063.statement: Philosophy is just abstract thinking and doesn’t apply to everyday life.
310917063.correction: Some people think philosophy is just for debates or theories, but Mary Midgley shows it’s actually a practical tool for thinking clearly about real issues like animal welfare.

225793930.belief: All Christians believe in original sin.
225793930.statement: That all Christians believe in original sin.
225793930.correction: Different Christian groups and individuals may believe in original sin or not and even those that do believe in it may have differing interpretations of what it actually means.

344766783.belief: All Christians view the song of Deborah as a supporting text for female leadership in religion.
344766783.statement: All Christians view the song of Deborah as a supporting text for female leadership in religion.
344766783.correction: There are different views on the leadership of women in religion; two examples are complementarian and egalitarian. These views will impact therefore how someone may view the song of Deborah in relation to supporting female leadership in religion.

486190818.belief: The story of Esther takes place in ancient Israel.
486190818.statement: That the story of Esther takes place in ancient Israel.
486190818.correction: The story of Esther takes place in Susa, an important city in the Persian Empire.

797824117.belief: The Immaculate Conception is when Mary conceived Jesus miraculously through the Holy Spirit.
797824117.statement: That the Immaculate Conception is when Mary conceived Jesus miraculously through the Holy Spirit.
797824117.correction: The Immaculate Conception is the Roman Catholic belief that Mary was born without sin. When the Angel Gabriel greets her for the first time she is called ‘Mary, full of Grace’, which would mean she was without sin even before Jesus is born.

752146475.belief: Paul's letters always oppose the leadership of women in Christianity.
752146475.statement: That Paul's letters always oppose the leadership of women in Christianity.
752146475.correction: Some letters can suggest this, but others commend women in various leadership positions in the Church.

732837151.belief: The Gospel of Mary is thought to be about Mary, the mother of Jesus.
732837151.statement: The Gospel of Mary is thought to be about Mary, the mother of Jesus.
732837151.correction: The Gospel of Mary is thought to be related to Mary Magdalene. There are other apocraphal writings in relation to Mary, the mother of Jesus, however, such as the Infancy Gospel of James and the Infancy Gospel of Thomas.

595882274.belief: Christianity spread from the Middle East to Europe and that is where the most ancient forms of Christianity began.
595882274.statement: Christianity spread from the Middle East to Europe and that is where the most ancient forms of Christianity began.
595882274.correction: The Coptic church shows that Christianity had spread to the continent of Africa many centuries before the impact of colonialism.

226707165.belief: African women’s experiences and theology can be adequately represented by either white women or African men.
226707165.statement: African women’s experiences and theology can be adequately represented by either white women or African men.
226707165.correction: African women have unique experiences and should share their own stories. Others can support them, but real representation comes from their own voices, not others speaking for them.

230491293.belief: Environmental activism and protest is primarily a European concern.
230491293.statement: Environmental activism and protest is primarily a European concern.
230491293.correction: Wangari Maathai blended her Catholic and Kikuyu beliefs to argue for environmental justice in Kenya. She framed this through a distinctively African theological lens.

767549340.belief: All saints canonised by the Roman Catholic Church are European.
767549340.statement: All saints canonised by the Roman Catholic Church are European.
767549340.correction: Saint Rose of Lima was the first saint to be canonised from the South American continent. She was Peruvian and is seen as a patron saint of indigenous peoples.

191160641.belief: Liberation is not always about escaping suffering.
191160641.statement: Liberation is not always about escaping suffering.
191160641.correction: Many Black women find strength in their faith and ability to survive hardship, not because God removes their suffering, but because His liberating presence sustains them.

832167487.correction: Candomblé is an ancient African faith shaped by enslavement. While some include Catholic elements for tradition or protection, many focus purely on African roots. It’s a living, evolving religion adapting to each generation’s needs.
